preconditions.expression: all(1 <= int(line.split()[0]) <= 100000 for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:]) and all(1 <= int(line.split()[1]) <= 100000 for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:]) and all(0 <= int(line.split()[2]) <= 10**18 for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:])
preconditions.description: Vertices are numbered from 1 to n (1 ≤ n ≤ 100 000), edges have non-negative integer weights (0 ≤ t ≤ 10^18), and no self-loops or multiple edges exist.

preconditions.expression: len(stdin.splitlines()) == m + 1 and all(len(line.split()) == 3 for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:])
preconditions.description: Input has exactly m + 1 lines: first line contains n and m, followed by m lines of edge descriptions.
First line of input contains integers n (vertices) and m (edges).

postconditions.description: Output is a non-negative integer representing the sum of all s values for interesting triples (u, v, s), modulo 10^9 + 7.

postconditions.expression: all(1 <= u < v <= n for u, v, s in interesting_triples) and all(s >= 0 for u, v, s in interesting_triples) and sum(s for u, v, s in interesting_triples) % (10**9 + 7) == int(stdout)
postconditions.description: For every interesting triple (u, v, s) where u < v, there exists a path between u and v such that the XOR of edge weights along the path equals s. The output is the sum of all such s values modulo 10^9 + 7.

postconditions.expression: interesting_triples == [(u, v, s) for u in range(1, n + 1) for v in range(u + 1, n + 1) for s in possible_s_values(u, v)]
postconditions.description: An interesting triple (u, v, s) exists if and only if there is a path from u to v where the XOR of edge weights equals s. `possible_s_values(u, v)` returns all such s values for the pair (u, v).

postconditions.expression: possible_s_values(u, v) == {xor_sum for path in all_paths(u, v) for xor_sum in compute_xor(path)}
postconditions.description: For a given pair (u, v), `possible_s_values(u, v)` is the set of all possible XOR sums of edge weights along any path from u to v, including non-simple paths.
